**TL;DR** — Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 on July 24 — frontier-class intelligence at half the price of comparable models, with a user-controlled effort dial and 1M-token context window, now the default in Claude Code.

## Anthropic and Claude

- **Claude Opus 5 launched July 24** — priced at $5/$25 per Mtok (same as Opus 4.8), but delivers benchmark results approaching Claude Fable 5 at roughly half that cost; ships with a per-request effort "dial" so users can trade capability for tokens, a 1M-token context window, and a Fast mode at 2.5× speed ($10/$50 per Mtok). [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/24/anthropic-releases-new-model-opus-5)

- **Claude Code v2.1.219 (Jul 24) ships Opus 5 as default** with three significant additions: subagent nesting now goes to depth 3 by default (was 1), `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` denies non-allowlisted hosts silently, and a new `DirectoryAdded` hook fires when `/add-dir` registers a new root mid-session. [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)

- **v2.1.218 (Jul 22)**: `/code-review` now runs as a background subagent; v2.1.217 added emoji shortcode autocomplete and fixed corporate mTLS/proxy settings being silently ignored in Desktop sessions; v2.1.216 fixed a quadratic slowdown in long sessions. [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)

- **Anthropic published its open-weights policy position (Jul 27)** — explicitly rejects bans; instead advocates chip export controls targeting China, crackdowns on state-backed industrial distillation operations, and mandatory pre-release safety testing for all sufficiently capable models regardless of weights status. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/position-open-weights-models)

## NixOS Ecosystem

- **Documentation team funding drive** (Jul 10) — the NixOS Foundation is soliciting donations to fund a renewed documentation team effort; the post outlines scope and how to contribute. [NixOS Blog](https://nixos.org/blog/announcements/2026/docs-funding-2026)

- **NixOS 26.05 "Yarara"** remains the current stable release (shipped May 30), carrying seven months of backported bugfix and security updates — no new stable release is imminent based on the blog. [NixOS Blog](https://nixos.org/blog/announcements/2026/nixos-2605)

- Nothing else new from nixos.org/blog in the last 7 days; the ecosystem appears in a quiet inter-release period.

## AI Coding Agents and Agent Frameworks

- **Supabase open-sourced `supabase/evals` on July 31** — an Apache-2.0 benchmark that runs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, GPT-5.6, Kimi K3) against real Supabase tasks in live containers with actual MCP + CLI; scoring combines deterministic checks with LLM-as-judge. Public leaderboard at supabase.com/evals. [Supabase](https://supabase.com/blog/introducing-supabase-evals)

- **Key evals finding**: Opus 5 and Kimi K3 both scored 100% on the Build stage with no pre-loaded skills; all agents struggled with declarative schema workflows, preferring manual migrations, and underutilized newer Supabase libraries — a useful signal for prompt engineering. [MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/01/supabase-releases-evals-an-open-source-benchmark-that-scores-claude-code-codex-and-opencode-on-real-supabase-tasks/)

- **EU AI Act compliance obligations** for high-risk agent frameworks took effect in August 2026, pushing governance and risk-management tooling up the priority stack for teams deploying agentic systems in Europe. (ongoing — multiple sources)

## Self-Hosting and Homelab

- **SharePoint zero-day CVE-2026-56164 actively exploited** — unauthenticated privilege-escalation in SharePoint Server was being weaponized in the wild at the time of July Patch Tuesday; CISA set an emergency patch deadline of July 17. Patch immediately if running on-prem SharePoint. [Self-Hosted Weekly, Week 29](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-29-2026-sharepoint-zero-day-nextcloud-migration-kvm-escape/)

- **KVM escape "Januscape" (CVE-2026-53359)** — a 16-year-old use-after-free in Linux kernel's KVM shadow MMU enables guest-to-host escape on both Intel and AMD; a second CVE (CVE-2026-46113) is required for full remediation. Critical for anyone running nested virtualization or multi-tenant VMs. [Self-Hosted Weekly, Week 29](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-29-2026-sharepoint-zero-day-nextcloud-migration-kvm-escape/)

- **Immich v3.0.0 and v3.1.0 released** — first major release since v2, adding mobile photo editing, workflow automation with asset/EXIF/upload-path filters, OIDC role sync, and undo-archive; shipped after four release candidates. [Immich Blog](https://immich.app/blog/2026-july-recap)

- **Forgejo v16.0 out July 16** — non-LTS release (supported through late October) with improved Git mirroring access controls and other security hardening. [Self-Hosted Weekly, Week 29](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-29-2026-sharepoint-zero-day-nextcloud-migration-kvm-escape/)

- **Minecraft Bedrock Dedicated Server CVE-2026-55010** — CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE; notable for homelab networks where game servers share a LAN segment. [Self-Hosted Weekly, Week 29](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-29-2026-sharepoint-zero-day-nextcloud-migration-kvm-escape/)

## Local and On-Device LLM Inference

- **Ollama v0.32.1 current as of July 16** — the v0.30–0.32 series brought llama.cpp alongside the MLX engine (Apple Silicon stays MLX-first), flash attention auto-enabled at runtime, smarter mixed quantization across dense and MoE layers, and NVFP4 Metal bug fixes that were reducing output quality on Laguna models. [Ollama release notes via releasebot.io](https://releasebot.io/updates/ollama)

- **Gemma 4 on MLX in Ollama 0.31 is ~90% faster** on a real coding-agent benchmark compared to prior Ollama versions — the biggest single-model speed improvement in the recent release series. [Explainx.ai](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/ollama-0-31-gemma-4-mtp-mlx-faster-coding-agents-2026)

- **ExecuTorch 1.0 GA** (Meta, reached GA October 2025 — flagging as ongoing state-of-play) — 50KB base footprint, 12+ hardware backends, 80%+ of top HuggingFace edge LLMs supported out of the box; now serving billions of users across Meta's apps. Relevant baseline for anyone building on-device pipelines. (ongoing)
